series_description: The cosmic visual storybook and planetary expedition chronicles of The Stardust Engine aboard the U.S.S. Aethelgard. Beginning inside the subterranean launch cavern beneath 'The Fortress' on Industrial Park Road in Blacksburg, Virginia (Movements I–III), Ryan, Cassidy, and Holly O'Connell—alongside twin pilots Tyler and Evan Wright—leave the fluorescent Cage of Earth behind, cross 1,200 light-years at FTL Harmonic Continuum speed, and step onto Caelum-IV (Movement IV, Stardate 49601): a 48-hour tidally locked, 0.88G purple-ocean moon orbiting the ringed super-Jovian Vespera (Kepler-442c) whose living biosphere pulses at 120.0 BPM.

parts.image_alt: Photorealistic widescreen view inside Subterranean Launch Silo Alpha 200 feet beneath Industrial Park Road in Blacksburg. The star-cruiser U.S.S. Aethelgard rests on hydraulic launch cradles over a misting flame trench as camouflaged quarry blast doors part overhead toward the starry Virginia night sky. In the foreground, mid-20s Ryan O'Connell propels his manual wheelchair toward the open aft boarding ramp with his hands on the wheel push-rims while his sister Cassidy O'Connell—who has cerebral palsy—holds onto the ergonomic rear push-handles of Ryan's wheelchair like a walker to steady her gait, followed by Holly O'Connell with her MagnaPad and twin cousins Tyler and Evan Wright in maroon CPI shirts.

parts.image_alt: Photorealistic widescreen view inside the forward cockpit of the U.S.S. Aethelgard during orbital ascent. Identical twin cousins Tyler and Evan Wright sit in the Port (Pilot) and Starboard (Copilot) leather flight seats wearing 5-point harnesses with their hands on dual flight sticks. Centered between them on the diamond-plate deck, mid-20s Ryan O'Connell sits in his manual wheelchair anchored by four heavy-duty floor ratchet tie-down straps and a 6-point aerospace chest harness over his maroon CPI shirt. Beside him, Cassidy O'Connell holds the overhead grab rail while steadying her left hand on Ryan's wheelchair push-handle, and Holly O'Connell monitors telemetry on her MagnaPad as Earth's blue horizon curves below the crimson-and-violet starfield.

parts.part_title: Part 1: Day 1 in the Continuum: Zero-G Hugs & Unbuckling the Tether
parts.location: Forward Cockpit & Panoramic Observation Lounge, U.S.S. Aethelgard — Deep-Space Continuum Transit (Day 1)
parts.image_alt: Photorealistic widescreen view inside the panoramic observation lounge of the U.S.S. Aethelgard during faster-than-light transit with artificial gravity set to 0.00G. On the diamond-plate deck in the lower foreground, Ryan's empty manual wheelchair (with its rear push-handles) remains anchored to the floor by four heavy-duty ratchet tie-down straps while its unbuckled 6-point harness straps float upward. Floating weightlessly in mid-air above the empty wheelchair in front of three panoramic nebula windows, mid-20s Ryan O'Connell shares a joyful zero-gravity group hug with his sisters Cassidy and Holly and his twin cousins Tyler and Evan in their maroon CPI shirts as guitar picks and sheet music drift around them.

parts.image_alt: Photorealistic widescreen view inside the onboard recording studio lounge of the U.S.S. Aethelgard during faster-than-light transit. Through the large panoramic windows on the left, a glowing crimson, gold, and violet nebula streams past in deep space. On the diamond-plate studio deck, mid-20s Ryan O'Connell sits in his manual wheelchair (secured by four floor ratchet tie-down straps and a 6-point harness, with rear push-handles) playing his cherry-sunburst solid-body electric guitar. Beside his wheelchair stands Cassidy O'Connell in her maroon CPI shirt and jeans, singing into a vintage condenser microphone while resting one hand lightly on Ryan's wheelchair push-handle for balance, as twins Evan and Tyler Wright play electric bass and drums and Holly O'Connell watches by the console.

parts.image_alt: Widescreen view from inside the open cargo hatch of the star-cruiser U.S.S. Aethelgard looking out onto the purple-sand beach and violet ocean of Caelum-IV. On the left, pilot twin Tyler/Evan Wright stands beside lead guitarist Ryan O'Connell in his custom manual wheelchair at the top of the landing ramp. Beside Ryan, lead vocalist Cassidy O'Connell holds a handheld frequency scanner and points out toward the bay in curiosity. On the right, manager Holly O'Connell stands by the starboard telemetry console with a datapad, keeping clear line-of-sight with her siblings. Outside, lavender bio-silica fronds and giant bioluminescent mushroom canopies frame a sky dominated by the ringed gas giant Vespera, its shepherd moons Lumen and Umbra, and the golden twilight of the orange dwarf star Solis-V.

parts.realm_time: Vespera Zenith • Lumen Ring-Shadow Transit (120.0 BPM Lock)

parts.image_alt: Photorealistic widescreen view on the dark purple-black basaltic beach of Caelum-IV beside the violet ocean under the ringed gas giant Vespera. Mid-20s Ryan O'Connell propels his manual wheelchair across the firm purple sand with his hands on the push-rims while his sister Cassidy O'Connell walks right beside him, resting one hand on Ryan's wheelchair push-handle like a walker to steady her cerebral palsy gait and holding a frequency scanner in her other hand. Beneath Ryan's tires and Cassidy's red sneakers, subterranean mycelial veins glow in crimson and cyan, flanked by 40-foot lavender bio-silica resonance fronds on the left and glowing violet Myco-Towers on the right.

parts.image_alt: Photorealistic widescreen view on the purple-sand beach of Caelum-IV during the Umbral Hush eclipse at the center of the 24-hour Ring-Night. Overhead, the orange sun is hidden directly behind the dark disk of the gas giant Vespera, rimming the giant planet in a blazing 360-degree halo of backlit golden-and-violet rings. Along the shoreline, the 40-foot lavender bio-silica fronds, giant Myco-Tower mushroom canopies, crimson-and-cyan mycelial root veins, and two breaching Vesperan Chorus-Rays glow in full bioluminescence around mid-20s Ryan O'Connell in his manual wheelchair, Cassidy O'Connell resting her hand on his wheelchair push-handle like a walker, Holly O'Connell, and twins Tyler and Evan Wright.
